Looking at this PR carefully:

1. **`app/serializers/user_serializer.rb`** - The new `def include_website_name` method is missing the `?` suffix. All other include predicate methods in this file (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`, `include_user_fields?`, etc.) correctly use the predicate form.

2. **`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb`** - The new `website_name` method has three branches but only two are tested. The `elsif` branch for same-segment-count subdomain matching (the `www.example.com == forum.example.com` case) is not covered.

3. **`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb`** - Edge cases for URL parsing aren't covered: malformed URLs, URLs without paths, URLs with trailing slashes (which produce different display text due to `URI().path` behavior).

findings.title: include_website_name missing ? suffix breaks AMS include check
findings.body: The new `def include_website_name` method at line 153 is missing the `?` suffix: it should be `def include_website_name?`. ActiveModel Serializers discovers conditional include logic by looking for predicate methods named `include_<attr>?` on the serializer. Without the `?`, this method is not recognized as an include check, and `website_name` will be included in the serialized JSON whenever the attribute method exists, regardless of whether `website` is set. This contradicts the design intent shown by the body `website.present?` and is inconsistent with every other `include_*?` method in the same file (e.g., `include_email?` at line 117, `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`, `include_user_fields?`, `include_topic_post_count?`), all of which correctly use the predicate form. Fixing this is a one-character change (`def include_website_name?`) and matches the established convention in the file.

findings.title: Missing test for same-segment-count subdomain (elsif) branch
findings.body: The `website_name` method has three branches: (1) exact host match `if website_host == discourse_host`, (2) same-segment-count subdomain match `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`, and (3) parent-domain match `else`. The three tests added in this PR only cover branches (1) and (3); the elsif branch (the `www.example.com == forum.example.com` case) is not exercised at all. That branch contains the most complex logic in the method — `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` — and has both a true and false outcome that should be verified, e.g., `Discourse.current_hostname = 'forum.example.com'` with website `http://www.example.com/user` (should yield `www.example.com/user`) and with website `http://www.other.com/user` (should yield `www.other.com`, no path).

findings.title: Missing edge case tests for URL parsing in website_name
findings.body: The new `website_name` method uses `URI(website.to_s).host` (with `rescue nil`) and `URI(website.to_s).path`, which behave inconsistently at the boundary. No tests cover: (1) a malformed URL such as `'not a valid url'` where `URI(...).host` raises (handled by `rescue nil`), (2) a URL with no path such as `http://example.com` where `URI().path` is `''`, producing `'example.com'`, or (3) a URL with a trailing slash such as `http://example.com/` where `URI().path` is `'/'`, producing `'example.com/'`. The trailing-slash inconsistency in particular means two visually identical URLs (one with, one without `/`) render different display text on the profile, which would surprise users and is worth either a test or explicit normalization in the serializer.
